question.text: The principle of 'tax neutrality' in AIF structuring means:

answer.text: The AIF itself pays no tax on any of its income.
All AIF income is taxed at the maximum marginal rate at the fund level.
SEBI guarantees a tax refund for all AIF investors every year.
The investor should not be in a WORSE tax position by investing through the AIF than by investing directly at the investor level.

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax neutrality means the pooling vehicle should not impose an additional tax cost that the investor would not face investing directly. In Cat I/II, this is achieved via Section 115UB pass-through for business/capital gains. In Cat III, MMR taxation at fund level still often achieves overall neutrality vs direct investing. The Trap: 'No tax at fund' overstates - Cat III AIFs ARE taxed at fund level. MMR-at-fund describes Cat III taxation, not 'neutrality'. SEBI refund claim is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: Taxation chapter (Ch 13) elaborates. XIX-A tests at distributor level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Draft the trust as determinate + irrevocable to preserve 115UB; losing pass-through is the single biggest tax-neutrality killer for a Cat I/II fund.
